records.finding: Step-table row 3 claimed cmd/shortfall's combined Querier reports Capabilities() as the AND of its two backends. It is a field-wise merge — Metrics and its history depth from the metric backend, Events and its depth from the event backend. A real AND over promql {Metrics:true,Events:false} and sql {Metrics:false,Events:true} yields {false,false}, under which every leg is ungrounded — so the claim falsified the very branch its next sentence explained.
records.evidence: Claim: 'Capabilities() is the **AND** of the two'. Code: cmd/shortfall/impact.go combined.Capabilities() returns query.Caps{Metrics: m.Metrics, Events: e.Events, MetricHistoryWeeks: m.MetricHistoryWeeks, EventHistoryWeeks: e.EventHistoryWeeks}; adapters/query/promql/promql.go Caps{Metrics:true,Events:false}; adapters/query/sql/sql.go Caps{Metrics:false,Events:true}. An AND gives {false,false}, and engine/realized.go falls through both cases to 'engine: realized leg needs an event or metric source; this backend serves neither'.
records.reason: Row 3 rewritten to state the field-wise merge, the {false,false} consequence, and that a single flag is what makes the realized leg's alt resolve either way. Round 2 verdicted addressed against cmd/shortfall/impact.go.

records.finding: Round 2, introduced by round 1's own fix to the same row: 'Every leg that has an Evidence field renders with its tag' is false for coverage in both text renderers, in exactly the case this diagram guarantees always occurs. records.evidence: Claim: 'Every leg that has an Evidence field renders with its tag'. Code: engine/engine.go Compute assigns report.Coverage = CoverageLeg{Evidence: EvidenceTrust, Unavailable: "coverage needs a provider ledger — run shortfall reconcile for the trust number"} unconditionally; engine/report/render.go RenderText prints 'COVERAGE   unavailable: %s' with no tag in that branch, and RenderMarkdown prints '_Unavailable: %s_'. Claim: 'An ungrounded money leg prints none'. Code: engine/report/render.go RenderJSON is json.MarshalIndent(r, "", "  ") with no json tags and no omitempty anywhere, so it emits the struct verbatim.
records.reason: Row 23 now states each renderer's behaviour per leg: the three money legs always tag, CustomersLeg has no Evidence field, coverage tags only when grounded, RenderJSON marshals verbatim with empty maps included. Round 3 verified all six clauses true and returned no new findings.

records.finding: The rewritten opening said 'only the four verbs' and then enumerated eight. In this repo 'the four verbs' is a term of art meaning the four METRIC verbs — c4-l1 and c4-l2 both write sum, count, group-by, range PLUS event order — so the sentence contradicted its own count and two diagrams stating the same standard.
records.evidence: Claim: 'the engine asks any backend only the four verbs — sum, count, group-by and time range over metrics, filter/group-by/order/distinct-count over events'. Contradicting artifacts: docs/architecture/c4-l1-context.md 'only four verbs: sum · count · group-by · range, plus event order' and c4-l2-containers.md 'the 4-verb AST ... sum · count · group-by · range + event order'. Both put the event side outside the count; the new sentence names four and enumerates eight.
records.reason: Restored to the c4-l1 wording: four named, four enumerated, event order carried outside the count. Round 2 confirmed all three files now agree.

Rule text: STYLE.md 5.2 '- Line 2 — the technology / module line. ... - No third line. A C4 node states its responsibilities because nothing else on the page does; a sequence participant's responsibilities are the messages on its own lifeline.' Its own example: 'participant EM as emit.Std
core module — Record buffers, Flush exports'. Refuting evidence: that example has exactly two lines, as do all 18 participants across the three governed diagrams, and STYLE.md section 6's checklist encodes the checkable form ('line 1 / line 2 in a sequence'), so no participant would be flagged.
records.reason: REFUTED by the cross-examiner. The normative rule is 'No third line' and every participant has exactly two. The sentence relied on is the stated REASON responsibilities get no line of their own, not a ban on a short gloss on line 2, and the section 6 checklist encodes the checkable form. At most rhetorical looseness, not a rule contradicted by its example.
